summary: Frontend regression testing after merging the Regex course into the app that already had Clojure and Web Dev courses. All requested flows work end-to-end with zero console errors/warnings. The three-course switcher lists all courses; each course loads its own content, has its own progress and lesson list, and its live execution paths (re-seq snippets for Regex, live Reagent for Web Dev, plain snippet + CTA for Clojure) work. Regex Golf → Leaderboard integration works: submitting #"(.)\1" passes HOLE 1, leaderboard golf-best-double shows 5 and golf-solved becomes 1/4; golf-reset clears back to — and 0/4.
verified_flows: Default load = Clojure course, title 'Parens — Learn Clojure', no console errors
course-switcher-btn opens course-switcher-menu with course-option-clojure, course-option-webdev, course-option-regex all present

Switch to Regex: title updates to 'Regex — Master Regular Expressions', sidebar brand shows '.* Regex / Master Regular Expressions', sidebar shows 18 lessons, sections 'Advanced Patterns' and 'Challenge' present
Regex nav-lesson-1 (find, seq & matches): 4 snippet-run buttons work; the re-seq digits example produces snippet-result => ("66" "99"), no snippet-error
Regex Golf (nav-lesson-15): typing #"(.)\1" into exercise-0 editor + exercise-check-0 → 'Solved / All checks passed', localStorage regex_golf_scores_v1 = {"double":5}
Leaderboard (nav-lesson-16): golf-leaderboard renders, golf-best-double = 5, golf-solved = '1/4 holes solved'
golf-reset clears to golf-best-double = '—' and golf-solved = '0/4 holes solved'

Switch to Web Dev: brand '</> Hiccup Web Dev with ClojureScript'; 'Hiccup: HTML as Data' lesson renders reagent-preview with content ('Hello, Hiccup!This is real HTML, described as a Clojure vector...'), no reagent-error
Switch back to Clojure: brand '( ) Parens Learn Clojure'; snippet-run → snippet-result '=> 42', no snippet-error
Per-course progress is independent (each course shows its own '0 of N lessons complete' and its own lesson list)
Console: 0 errors, 0 warnings across all flows (only informational React DevTools tip)
notes_for_e1: Testability nit (not a blocker): The Exercise editor does not expose a data-testid (e.g. exercise-editor-0). The task spec implied one. Playwright had to reach into [data-testid="exercise-0"] .cm-content and use keyboard.insert_text to bypass CodeMirror's auto-close-quote behavior when typing #"(.)\1". Consider adding data-testid="exercise-editor-<i>" on the CodeMirror wrapper for easier automation.
Testability nit: sidebar brand (Regex '.* Regex' / '</> Hiccup' / '( ) Parens') has no data-testid="sidebar-brand"; verified visually and via the first ~80 chars of the sidebar's innerText.
critical_code_review_comments: No critical issues found for the merge. LessonView 'golf-board' + Exercise -> golf.recordGolfScore + GolfLeaderboard reset flow behaves correctly, and localStorage key 'regex_golf_scores_v1' is written/cleared as expected.
seed_data_creation: None. localStorage was cleared at start of each run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Course-switch-with-three-courses merge is green. When automating Regex Golf exercises, use page.keyboard.insert_text('#"(.)\\1"') after Ctrl+A/Backspace inside [data-testid="exercise-0"] .cm-content; page.keyboard.type triggers CodeMirror's auto-close-quote and produces #"(.)\1\"" which fails the checks. nav-lesson-N is 0-indexed against the lesson list, so Regex nav-lesson-15 = 'Regex Golf' (sidebar number 16) and nav-lesson-16 = 'Capstone: Golf Leaderboard' (sidebar number 17).
rca of the issue: No functional bug. Only an automation caveat documented above.
